title: Teachers and appreciating a single note
summary: Thomas links the Prince Robinson story back to Langford and Olivieri, saying it is about appreciating what the writer wants, which is how he and Henderson understood each other.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: We'd get these little tape things together so we wanted to tape our tunes naturally. What the hell, I mean, that's the purpose. So I'd sing some Louis Armstrong (?) and said, That's the way to do it. We didn't tape one record of ours. Reminds me of a story that this Prince Robinson, maybe you've heard of him. He worked for a band called the Cotton pickers.

McKinney's Cottonpickers, that was the name in those days. That's just as plain as that was. So, back to Mr. Olivierri Langford teaching and Olivierri, Anton Olivierri ... and young people I've met and the great musicians that I've met along the way but they're talking a lot of things. But the

thing that could happen really and truly I think was appreciated of that one note, appreciating what the guy is writing. Now the difference comes with a bit of knowledge. The guy knows, well, look that's what I said. Now you can't show me. That's where I think Henderson and I always got together.
